subject: Renewal: Solara Systems - staged commit increase + temporary rate hold
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@solarasys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal: staged commit increase + temporary rate hold

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for the demo last week. I pulled together a clean renewal path that we think balances Solara's forecasted growth with price predictability while keeping your monthly spend from spiking in Q3. High level:

- 12-month renewal (starts 2027-07-01)
- Staged commit increase: 1.0M tokens/month for months 1–3, 1.5M for months 4–9, 2.0M months 10–12
- Temporary rate hold: lock current effective per-token rate for the first 6 months of the renewal (we apply true-up at month 7 if usage exceeds staged commits)
- One-time usage credit: $35k applied as invoice credit at renewal start to offset migration/engineering uplift

I attached a short addendum and a concession matrix that maps potential volume ramps to credit sizing. If that structure works, we can produce an addendum for signature and offer a 30-day window to lock the rates.

Questions for you:
1) Does procurement need the addendum in PDF or Word?
2) Is the staged ramp aligned with the plans you shared (50%+ growth in Q4)?
3) Can your procurement/legal review within two weeks so we can finalize ahead of your fiscal close?

If yes, I’ll loop in our legal and finance contacts to produce the DocuSign packet.

Thanks —
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment(s): Solara - Commitment Addendum.pdf, Concession_Matrix.xlsx
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@solarasys.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@solarasys.com>, Michael Tran <michael.tran@solarasys.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: staged commit increase + temporary rate hold

Hi Sofia —

Appreciate the clear layout. The staged ramp looks sensible to the product team; our only ask is a firmer guarantee on the 6-month price hold so our finance team can commit to the numbers for the board. A couple notes from procurement:

- Please provide the addendum in Word (procurement redlines faster there).
- The $35k credit is welcome; can we split it as $20k applied at renewal start and $15k applied as a mid-term credit at month 6 tied to adoption milestones?
- Our preferred contract language: a one-time rate-lock clause listing exact SKU rates and a capped true-up equal to 120% of the staged commit for the first true-up period.

Michael (cc) wants an estimate of downside protection if we exceed the staged ramp (i.e., what's the emergency overage rate and how would credits apply).

If you can get the Word addendum and a short confirmation of the split credit + rate-lock language, we can move to signature.

Thanks —
Aisha
Aisha Patel | Head of Cloud Products
Solara Systems
aisha.patel@solarasys.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Solara request - guidance on split credit and true-up cap

Sofia / Rishi —

Saw Aisha's asks. Quick take from pricing/legal POV:

- Splitting the $35k credit as $20k / $15k tied to adoption milestones is OK from a margin perspective if we make the second tranche contingent (e.g., 75% of expected active endpoints or 60% of forecasted token throughput) — we should write the milestone criteria tight.
- Rate-lock language: we can offer a 6-month explicit rate-lock on the effective per-token price; beyond month 6, true-up can happen but cap the emergency overage rate to 1.6x of the locked rate for the remainder of Q3 (to avoid open-ended exposure).
- The staged commit multiples and the 120% capped true-up look reasonable; legal will want to see the exact SKU/units called out.

Action items:
1) Sofia: produce .docx addendum with the split-credit language and explicit SKU rates (I can drop in the emergency overage clause).
2) Rishi: please pre-authorize the $35k credit structure so finance can sign off (I can route the concession if you approve).

Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Sales Manager, Enterprise
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment(s): Concession_Matrix.xlsx (internal comments)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@solarasys.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@solarasys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: staged commit increase + temporary rate hold

Aisha —

Thanks for the quick turn. Attached is a Word addendum that reflects:
- $20k credit applied to invoice at renewal start; $15k paid as a credit at month 6 tied to the adoption milestone (we listed the milestone threshold in section 2)
- 6-month rate-lock clause with explicit per-token rates for the committed SKUs (see table)
- True-up language: initial true-up at month 7 with cap at 120% of staged commit; emergency overage ceiling capped at 1.6x the locked per-token rate through the remainder of Q3.

I also generated the DocuSign packet so procurement can sign the addendum; link below. If procurement wants any redlines, I'll accept tracked changes in the Word file and we can iterate quickly.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/doc/abcdef1234567890

If this is good, we can sign and I’ll route to finance to apply the $20k credit at the July invoice and queue the $15k mid-term credit pending milestone verification.

Best —
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
